newsitem.title: UK: UK greenhouse gas emissions now rising - report.
newsitem.headline: UK greenhouse gas emissions now rising - report.

text.p: Britain's emissions of greenhouse gases are on the rise, making a U.K. target to combat global warming look out of reach without strong new measures, a leading consultancy said on Monday.
"Carbon emissions are projected to rise over the next five to ten years largely due to growing road transport and power generation demand," Cambridge Econometrics said in a report released on Monday.
Britain is committed to cutting its emissions of carbon dioxide, the main greenhouse gas, by 20 percent from 1990 levels by 2010 and said sweeping lifestyle changes would be needed to hit the target.
Prime Minister Tony Blair will lead the call at a summit in December of industrialised nations in Kyoto in favour of a tough new target for legally binding reductions in greenhouse gases.
Cambridge Econometrics' report said that by 2010 UK emissions are expected to be less than four percent below 1990 levels. Under current government policy emissions would only start to fall by 2008.
And indications from the Labour government that it might encourage coal power stations using new clean technology could further hamper reductions, the report said.
"The use of clean coal-fired generation by the electricity supply industry could reduce by half the CO2 emissions saved from a programme to get 10 percent of generation from renewables," it said.
The government has admitted that without further steps carbon dioxide emissions in Britain will be slightly higher than they were in 1990.
It has suggested more bus lanes, energy efficiency schemes and improved traffic management.
